title: Vowel-Bounded Words per Range
statement:
You get a list of lowercase words words and a list of queries. Each query is [l, r] with 0 ≤ l ≤ r < words.length.

Call a word vowel-bounded if its first letter and its last letter are both vowels (a, e, i, o, u). A one-letter word counts when that letter is a vowel. The letter y is not a vowel here.

For each query, count the vowel-bounded words with an index from l to r, both ends included. Return the counts in the order of the queries.

examples.why: "echo", "idea" and "a" qualify. "oxen" starts with a vowel but ends with "n", so the last query counts nothing.
"bob" is skipped because its ends are consonants, even though it has a vowel inside.

hints: Each query asks how many marked items lie in a range. Re-counting every range from scratch is O(n) per query.
Mark each word with 1 if it is vowel-bounded and 0 otherwise. A range count is then a range sum.
Build prefix sums: pre[i] = number of vowel-bounded words among the first i words. The answer to [l, r] is pre[r + 1] − pre[l].

explain.intuition:
The word test is cheap: look at two letters. The expensive part is that there can be 100 000 queries over 100 000 words, so recounting each range costs up to 1010 steps.

Turn the words into a 0/1 array and precompute running totals. A prefix-sum array answers "how many in [l, r]" with one subtraction, the same way a table footer can show a running total without re-adding every row each time a filter changes.
steps: For each word i, set pre[i + 1] = pre[i] + 1 if its first and last letters are vowels, otherwise pre[i + 1] = pre[i].
For each query [l, r], output pre[r + 1] − pre[l].
pitfalls: Off by one in the prefix lookup: pre[r] − pre[l] drops word r, and pre[r + 1] − pre[l − 1] reads index −1 for l = 0.
Checking only the first letter, or checking whether the word contains any vowel.

solutions.title: Count every range directly
solutions.idea: For each query, walk the range and test every word.

solutions.title: Prefix sums
solutions.idea: Running totals of vowel-bounded words make every range count a single subtraction.

followups: Words can also be replaced between queries. Which structure keeps both updates and range counts at O(log n)?
Queries arrive as a stream and the words list keeps growing at the end. Does the prefix array still work?
